godzilla minus zero|.summary: Staggering effects and thrilling set-pieces outweigh overcooked, clichéd drama and hammy dialogue; still the most confident vision of Godzilla.
Devastating human drama and spectacular kaiju action make it bigger than Minus One and one of the year's best films.
A near-perfect sequel that surpasses Minus One with stunning IMAX spectacle, compelling human drama, and strong performances.
Stunning visuals can't save diluted human stories, an unearned ending, and a dumbed-down, remarkably mediocre sequel.
A visually stunning, emotionally rich sequel with blockbuster spectacle done right, though shaggier and less focused than Minus One.
Though less poignant than Minus One, it delivers awe-inspiring kaiju spectacle grounded in genuine post-war tragedy and strong human drama.

the mongoose|.summary: Silly plot and clunky dialogue, but propulsive pacing and excellent practical stunt work make it an above-average Neeson actioner.
The critic calls it a silly, sentimental action movie, suggesting a dismissive take on Liam Neeson's veteran-on-the-run vehicle.
Real stunt driving has moments, but redundant chases, clunky exposition, and thin characters leave the movie with little of anything.
Decent car stunts can't save an atrocious, lazy script; the critic calls it a bad movie, though unintentionally fun.
A mildly positive 2.5 stars: the car chases and stunts slap, though the dialogue is clumsy and the Afghanistan flashbacks are hack writing.

the only living pickpocket in new york|.summary: Praises Turturro's controlled performance, authentic New York locations, strong ensemble, and a restrained, humane crime story bridging old and new.
A character-driven, 1970s-style drama anchored by Turturro's weary, determined performance and an affecting air of mourning for obsolescence.
Praises Turturro's magnificent, humane performance, strong supporting cast, Sam Levy's New York cinematography, and Noah Segan's moving take on caregiving.
Enjoyable but disposable: Turturro and the lovingly shot New York charm, though the character study is shallow and derivative.
John Turturro gives the most lived-in, marvelous performance of his career in a heartbreaking, quintessentially New York movie.
Praises Turturro's performance as one of his best, plus the gritty 1970s atmosphere and the bittersweet portrait of a vanishing New York.
Despite occasional sentimentality, Segan's affection for old New York and its beloved character actors, led by Turturro, proves irresistible.
Turturro gives an awards-worthy lead performance, backed by a strong supporting cast and authentic New York location shooting.
The critic calls John Turturro's lead performance as an aging thief dynamite, signaling a positive take; only the listing blurb was available.
Turturro's beguiling, near career-best performance anchors a delicate, authentic New York crime mood piece the critic calls a low-key charmer.
John Turturro is magnificent in Noah Segan's tender, funny, nostalgic ode to old New York, an authentic, thrilling and wholesome caper.
A sharply paced, affectionate New York crime thriller anchored by one of John Turturro's very best, nuanced performances.
Familiar New York settings and an overstuffed genre mix, but well-written, well-acted characters, Turturro's subtle turn, and plenty of heart.
An understated, expertly paced crime drama about aging and dignity, anchored by one of John Turturro's most affecting performances.
John Turturro's soulful performance and the film's textured New York atmosphere make it charming, despite a miscast villain and thin impact.
An affectionate salute to the old New York indie crime film, likened to Peckinpah's wistful last ride for beloved veterans.
Segan gives Turturro the role of a lifetime in a cleverly constructed, emotionally powerful crime tale destined for cult status.
Praises Turturro's Oscar-worthy performance, a classy cast, and Segan's wistful, loving portrait of New York despite a predictable plot.
A sparkling, gently sad debut from Noah Segan, anchored by John Turturro's elegant, resigned performance, despite a weaker final stretch.
Segan blends thriller pacing with a love letter to NYC, giving Turturro his best showcase since 'Quiz Show.'
A charming, nimble, affecting drama with remarkable lightness of touch, anchored by one of John Turturro's finest performances.

wicker|.summary: Though the premise feels stretched and the ensemble underserved, Colman and Skarsgård are irresistibly weird and wonderful, backed by crisp visuals.
A caustic yet ultimately sincere fable about human flaws, anchored by a pure, decent wicker husband and sharp humor.
Smutty, silly, delightful romp with an astonishing practical wicker suit and strong cast, though its ideas about love are thin.
Ribald medieval comedy with romance and heart, memorable Colman, strong supporting cast, and a captivating whimsical score.
An irreverent, sweet, horny fable with a great cast and craft that genuinely challenges traditional marriage without a vanilla ending.
Quirky gender-role parody with a tender heart and strong final 30 minutes, though sometimes one-joke and with underdeveloped supporting characters.
A smart, witty, feminist fairytale with a tender love story and excellent performances, especially from Colman and Skarsgård.
A delightful, beautifully crafted fairy-tale social satire with a bawdy, charming Olivia Colman, astounding wicker makeup, and genuine heart.
Praises Colman and Skarsgård's performances, deft tonal balance, and extraordinary craftwork; calls it the critic's favorite film of Sundance 2026.
Funny, filthy, tender and original, with a magnificent Colman, sharp jokes, and genuine heart about love and acceptance.
A sexy, affecting adult fairy tale with excellent Colman and Skarsgård performances and remarkable practical effects; unusual and rewarding.
A delightful, bawdy, poetic fairytale fable with Colman's masterful performance and Skarsgård sensational as the wicker man.
Wildly original, hilarious fairy-tale fable with superb performances from Colman and Skarsgård, stunning practical effects, and sharp social satire.
A buoyant, bitter, sexy and funny fairy tale with delightful Colman and a strong comic cast that remembers fairy tales are scary.
Balances comedy and drama better than its pairing, with impressive practical wicker effects and a delightful Olivia Colman, though townsfolk subplots drag.
An absurd premise works thanks to a committed cast, self-aware fairy-tale tone, and a surprisingly sweet, profound take on love and empowerment.
A witty, raunchy, beautifully acted fable about marriage and envy, with a clever script and emotionally resonant climax.
Despite an excellent cast and colorful world, the fable-thin characters and retreat into cutesiness leave it well-constructed but hollow.
Colman and Skarsgård bring genuine humor and heart to a wonderfully weird, beautifully shot fable with extravagant empathy and magic.
Despite overcooked broad comedy and a weak script, strong performances, gothic touches, and craftsmanship make it a worthwhile offbeat oddity.
A masterfully handled, witty satirical fairy tale with magical performances from Colman and Skarsgård and an excellent supporting cast.
The critic calls it a wonderfully raunchy satire about a willow-branch man upending a rigid rural village.
A sexy, satirically funny, haunting fable with a superb Olivia Colman, a strong cast and exquisite craft; the year's most unexpected charmer.
A weird but genuinely romantic fairy tale anchored by Colman's distinguished performance, despite overbearing humor and pacing lulls.
A mischievous, crowd-pleasing, sharply made folktale with rich ideas and a nimble Colman, despite thin characters and skipped emotional beats.
Colman and Skarsgård charm and the romance is wonderful, but the rushed, moralistic back half squanders the film's potential.
The critic appreciates how the bawdy adult fable brings childlike sincerity to its mature themes, with Skarsgård a sturdy presence.
A darkly funny, surprisingly moving adult fairy tale with an effervescent Colman, devoted Skarsgård, and disarming handling of insecurity.
A charming, sensual romantic fantasy anchored by Colman's touching performance and sharp community critique; flaws are minor hiccups.
A warm, charming fable with real pathos, elevated by Olivia Colman's exemplary performance and striking craft, despite heavy-handed themes.
A hilarious, heartfelt raunchy fairy tale with an impeccable Colman, sharp gender-role satire, and magical production design.
Fun, fresh, bawdy fable with superb production design and one of Colman's best roles, though the third act loses momentum.
A satisfying grown-up fairy tale, funny without cruelty, poignant, with a strong cast; one of the year's most winning unexpected pleasures.
A brilliant, beautiful, honest romance with a glowing Olivia Colman, extraordinary practical makeup, and sweeping passion, likened to Her.
Colman and a wicker Skarsgård share wonderful chemistry in a beautifully crafted, hilarious, thoughtful fable, despite a forced late conflict.
A beautifully constructed fable with committed, delightfully strange performances from Colman and Skarsgård, gorgeous design, and a heartfelt message about mutual love.
Despite a concept stretched thin and fading humor, Colman and an able ensemble make this bawdy fairy tale a merry cinematic treat.
Entertaining, saucy fable elevated by Colman and Skarsgård's committed performances and impressive Wētā practical effects, despite one-note humour.
Olivia Colman dazzles in a warm, romantic folk fable with a charming village, though its moral is trite and it feels stretched.
A charming, bold, sexy adult fable with Olivia Colman, layered and witty, though it loses some steam after a fabulous first act.
An intriguing, peculiar folk-horror romance blending macabre and sentimental, with a fierce Colman and droll supporting performances.
Marvellous craftsmanship and prosthetics, but passive protagonists, hit-and-miss humour and meandering, heavy-handed storytelling leave it hollow.
An on-the-nose first act and unprofound messages hold it back, but makeup effects and a strong ending make it memorable.
A strange, heartfelt, unapologetically romantic fairy tale with Oscar-worthy makeup and a genuine love story between unlikely partners.
Mostly about the 4DX screening, but she calls the film moving, funny and bawdy, a cathartic celebration of female desire.
Headline calls the film a muddled mess of necessary feminism, sociology, and cheap sexuality, signaling a negative take.
A strange, charming fable with sharp satire on hypocrisy, wickedly funny and moving, elevated by Olivia Colman and a wonderful cast.
A delightful, bawdy, smart fairy tale with sharp gender satire and excellent performances, despite one unconvincing second-act subplot.
A sweet, bawdy comedy with astounding practical effects bringing Alexander Skarsgård's kindly wicker hunk to life.
A delightful, funny fairy-tale romcom with superb makeup effects, a witty farcical script, and a heartwarming central romance between Colman and Skarsgård.
Headline praises Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgard as shining in a wicked, strange love story; rated 3.5 stars.
A smart, beautifully woven fairy-tale love story with a perfectly cast Skarsgård and delicate Colman, despite uneven pacing and tone.
An enchanting, genre-bending adult fairy tale with beautiful craft and a compelling Olivia Colman, despite occasionally over-explicit dialogue.
A joyously bawdy, unexpected fairy tale remix with a game cast that blends outrageous humor with poignant themes of class and mortality.
A delightfully deranged, fully realised adult fairytale with a committed cast, superb wicker effects, and an open-hearted, sex-positive love story.
A charming, witty fable elevated by Colman and Skarsgård's chemistry, though its feather-light touch slightly blunts emotional highs.
A sly, ribald feminist fable elevated by Skarsgård's tender performance, amazing creature effects, and a skilled comic cast, despite simplistic satire.
